title: Google’s Fitbit Edge Debuts a Replaceable Battery—and Brings Back the Screen
gist: Google announced the $180 Fitbit Edge, a screen-equipped fitness tracker with a user-replaceable battery, 1.34-inch display, GPS, ECG sensors, Gemini-based automatic workout detection and iPhone/Android support, going on sale October 27. Wired notes the omission of NFC contactless payments and seven-day battery life, positioning it between basic Fitbits and the Pixel Watch.

insights.claim: Google's Fitbit Edge, priced at $180 with preorders open and sale starting October 27, is a pill-shaped screen-equipped tracker positioned between cheaper Fitbits and the costlier Pixel Watch, and works with both Android and iPhones via the Google Health app.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Cross-platform support and a mid-price slot widen Google's wearables addressable market beyond Pixel owners.
insights.quote: It sits in a sweet spot at $180—not as costly as a Google Pixel Watch
insights.locator: Announced on Monday, it is the successor

insights.claim: The Edge succeeds the three-year-old Charge 6 with a larger 1.34-inch display versus 1.04 inches, newer automatic workout detection, deeper health metrics and an IP68 rating, and brings back a screen after the screenless Fitbit Air.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Google is rebuilding the Fitbit line around both screenless and screen products after a long refresh gap.
insights.quote: it’s been three years since the company updated its display-equipped Charge 6

insights.claim: The Edge has a user-replaceable battery, a Fitbit first, consistent with efforts to make the Pixel Watch more repairable and likely driven partly by new EU battery regulations taking effect next year.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: EU battery rules are pushing consumer hardware makers toward replaceable batteries, affecting design and repair costs.
insights.quote: (Likely also due to new battery regulations set to take effect next year in the European Union.)

insights.claim: Google's Gemini Intelligence identifies up to 100 workout types and the Edge tracks more than 50 exercise modes, up from 40, with the features also coming to Pixel Watch 5 and the Air.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Embeds Gemini in wearables, a distribution channel for Google's AI beyond phones.
insights.quote: Google also announced more advanced automatic activity tracking for the Edge, using Gemini Intelligence
insights.locator: Google also announced more advanced automatic

insights.claim: With a Google Health Premium subscription, the Edge can track blood pressure trends without manual calibration and insulin resistance trends without a blood draw, features that became available only at the end of September.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Subscription-gated health features indicate Google's push for recurring wearable revenue.
insights.quote: blood pressure trends without manual calibration and insulin resistance trends without requiring a blood draw
insights.locator: With a Google Health Premium subscription

insights.claim: The Edge borrows an altimeter and a far-field skin temperature sensor from the Pixel Watch and restores built-in GPS and ECG-capable electrical sensors that the screenless Air lacks.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Upmarket sensors in a $180 device raise competitive pressure on rivals' fitness trackers.
insights.quote: The Edge borrows a few more attributes from the Pixel Watch
insights.locator: The Edge borrows a few more

insights.claim: Battery life stays at seven days with about 90 minutes to fully charge, 30 minutes faster than Charge 6, but the Edge lacks NFC and therefore Google Wallet contactless payments, a downgrade from the Charge 6.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Missing payments is a notable feature gap that may dampen appeal for some buyers.
insights.quote: One odd omission is a near-field communication (NFC) sensor

insights.claim: Google will give the Fitbit Air a Metal Mesh band, and the Edge ships with a range of band styles including a $220 Stephen Curry collaboration, using accessories to turn the screenless tracker into a fashion item.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Accessory sales are a minor, high-margin add-on to wearables.
insights.locator: The Edge introduces new digital and analog
